value.tagline: Dorren Skura moves to Chicago, goes 16-1 and edges the Dolphins 40-38 in Super Bowl CLVII for an eighth straight title, JJ Starling throws 61 touchdown passes for the MVP in his first season, and Ryland Maxwell enters the Hall of Fame.

articles.headline: Eight Straight, New Colors: Skura's Bears Edge the Dolphins 40-38 in Super Bowl CLVII
articles.dek: Dorren Skura left Philadelphia after seven straight titles, went 16-1 in Chicago and won another with a roster built almost entirely of first-year players.
body: The address changed. The ending did not. After seven straight championships in Philadelphia, Dorren Skura took over a Bears club that had gone 11-6 in Y97, and Chicago went 16-1. The only loss came in week 5, 25-22 at Green Bay. The Bears then won their last 12 regular-season games, beat the Giants 46-25 and the Commanders 40-29 at home, and held off the Dolphins 40-38 in Super Bowl CLVII. It is Skura's eighth straight title across two clubs, and the first Super Bowl the Bears have ever won.

It was not a dominant team on paper. Chicago outscored its opponents by 130 points, fewer than the Ravens' 147, and its 424 points allowed were the fewest in the league by a modest margin. What the Bears did was win close games: 10-1 in one-score games in the regular season. By points scored and allowed they were an 11-win team. They won 16.

The roster was new almost to a man. JJ Starling, 23, threw 61 touchdown passes in his first season and was named MVP. Ken Strange caught passes for 2,080 yards, Makai Singer ran for 1,688 and won Offensive Player of the Year, and Harvey Ratley was Super Bowl MVP. The thread back to the old dynasty was Snoop Dotson, who followed Skura from Philadelphia, won a 9th ring and finished with more career sacks than anyone on league cards.

The final was Skura's closest Super Bowl win since his Jets beat Seattle 28-26 in Y80. Miami, 5-12 a year earlier, came within 2 points behind Brandon Jaclyde, the 38-year-old who quarterbacked Skura's Falcons to the Y83 title. The dynasty survived the move. Whether a lineup this young can carry it is the question for Y99.

articles.headline: 61 Touchdowns, 20 Interceptions and an MVP: The Case For and Against JJ Starling
articles.dek: Chicago's first-year quarterback led the league in touchdown passes and in interceptions, and the market still prices his card at 32.
body: No quarterback has arrived like this in years. JJ Starling, 23, threw for 5,019 yards and 61 touchdowns in 20 games, completed 310 of 363 passes, 85.4%, and was named MVP in his first season on league cards. The next best touchdown total belonged to the Rams' Makai Merritt, with 43. Starling ran for 8 more.

The other column is harder to ignore. His 20 interceptions were the most in the league, double Seattle's Julian Goedert and far more than the 3 Bones Crawford threw in Philadelphia. A year ago Crawford threw 64 touchdown passes for the same coach. Starling's line reads like a quarterback who throws every ball he likes and lets a 2,080-yard receiver sort it out.

The market has not bought in. His card carries an overall rating of 66 and a value of 32, a sliver of the 24,847 that Crawford's commands. The skill grade is already A+, but the record is one season long. If Starling cuts the interceptions in half, that price will not last.

articles.headline: Strange 2,080, Ratley 1,747, Smoke 19 Touchdowns: Chicago's First-Year Weapons
articles.dek: Ken Strange was Offensive Rookie of the Year, Harvey Ratley the Super Bowl MVP and Makai Singer Offensive Player of the Year, all in their first seasons.
body: Philadelphia's two-receiver offense stayed behind when Skura left. Chicago built a new one at once. Ken Strange, 21, caught 113 passes for 2,080 yards and 20 touchdowns, the most yards in the league, 333 more than his own teammate. That teammate, Harvey Ratley, also 21, had 1,747 yards and was named Super Bowl MVP. The best receiver outside Chicago, the Rams' Cooper Grigsby, finished with 1,074.

Tight end Kristian Smoke caught 19 touchdowns on 70 receptions, a score on 27.1% of his catches. Makai Singer ran for 1,688 yards, second in the league to Washington's Alijah Santos, and was named Offensive Player of the Year. Up front, Grant Isidora, 21, made 39 blocks, the most by any lineman and 6 more than Green Bay's Cordale Sweezy.
Every one of them played all 20 of Chicago's games, and none had played a league game before Y98.

articles.headline: Snoop Dotson Follows Skura to Chicago and Takes the Sack Lead With Him
articles.dek: The 32-year-old linebacker added 3 sacks and a 9th ring, and his 26 career sacks are now the most on any league card.
body: When Dorren Skura moved to Chicago, one piece of the Philadelphia defense moved with him. Snoop Dotson, 32, played all 20 of the Bears' games, made 85 tackles, intercepted a pass and recorded 3 sacks, tied for the most in the league.

That settled a race a year in the making. Dotson began Y98 at 23 career sacks, 1 behind the 24 that Deshone Bello and Kalif Suh share. He finished at 26, the most on any player's career card. Only the 112 on Skura's record board, a club mark that has stood since Y6, is higher.

The rings kept coming as well. His 9th came in his first season away from the Eagles, and the market took notice: his card value rose 112% to 24,593. The Hall of Fame watch now scores him at 97, well above the bar of 65. For a linebacker who spent years in the shadow of Philadelphia's offense, Chicago has been a fine place to be the veteran in the room.

articles.headline: Jaclyde at 38: The Dolphins Go From 5-12 to 2 Points Short of a Title
articles.dek: Miami's quarterback won a ring with Skura's Falcons in Y83 before the trade that sent him south. In Super Bowl CLVII he nearly took one from his old coach.
body: Brandon Jaclyde has been a Dolphin since Y84, the season after he quarterbacked Dorren Skura's Falcons to a title and was traded to Miami. Miami did not reach a Super Bowl in any of the seasons between. Then, at 38, he led a team that had gone 5-12 in Y97 to a 9-8 record and a playoff run that ended only in the final, a 40-38 loss to Skura's Bears.

Jaclyde threw 36 touchdown passes and only 5 interceptions in 21 games. Lukas Agnew, 33, ran for 1,416 yards and 29 touchdowns, and tight end Eli Danna, 34, caught 99 passes. The market moved on all of them: Danna's card rose 230% and Jaclyde's climbed from 574 to 771.

There is history in the loss. Every Super Bowl the Dolphins have won came with Skura as their coach, the last of them in Y59. Miami's finals in Y21 and Y37 were lost to his Buccaneers and his Seahawks. No club had come as close to beating him in a Super Bowl since Seattle in Y80, and it still was not enough.

articles.headline: Life After Skura: The Eagles Go 13-4 and Exit After One Playoff Game
articles.dek: Bones Crawford's touchdown passes nearly halved, Payton Jarrett fell from 2,007 yards to 304, and the seven-time defending champions watched the final from home.
body: Philadelphia did not collapse. The Eagles went 13-4, outscored their opponents by 120 points and finished third in the power rankings. For most clubs that is a fine season. For a club that had won the last seven titles, it was the end of something: one playoff game, one loss, and the trophy went to Skura's new club instead.

The passing game took the hardest hit. Bones Crawford, 33, threw 35 touchdown passes, down from 64, though he was intercepted only 3 times. Calvin Wingo II fell from 2,158 receiving yards to 749. Payton Jarrett, a 2,007-yard receiver in Y97, caught 65 passes for 304 yards, 4.7 a catch.

There were bright spots. DeSean Fries, 21, ran for 1,496 yards and 25 touchdowns in his first season, though he fumbled 13 times. Akiem Brock, 35, made 28 blocks in 18 games. But Crawford's card slipped from 25,496 to 24,847, and the roster that won seven straight is largely still there. The coach is not, and the difference showed.

articles.headline: Mad Max and Brooker Walk Into the Hall of Fame on the First Ballot
articles.dek: Ryland Maxwell retired with 33,955 rushing yards and 14 rings; Jamon Brooker with 47 interceptions and no ring at all. Both were voted in at once.
body: The Class of Y98 is small, and the vote was not close. Ryland Maxwell goes in with a Hall of Fame score of 100, the maximum, and Jamon Brooker with 97, both far above the bar of 65 and both in their first year on the ballot.

Maxwell's case needs no argument. He retired after Y97 with 33,955 career rushing yards, the league record, and 440 rushing touchdowns, the most on Skura's record board but 18 short of Lane McCoy's league mark of 458. That chase is over, and McCoy keeps it. Maxwell also took 14 rings, every one with Dorren Skura, and 8 Super Bowl MVPs, and his card, at 50,066, is still the most valuable in the game.

Brooker's career ran the other way. He played all 266 of his games for Green Bay, won Defensive Player of the Year twice and finished with 47 interceptions, the most on any league card and 4 clear of Damar Hobbs and Lewis Pettis. He never won a ring. The voters did not hold it against him.

articles.headline: Hoyer Closes to 77 Tackles of Swaim, and McCoy's Touchdown Mark Survives
articles.dek: A.T. Hoyer made 222 tackles for the Raiders and is chasing two career records at once. Akayleb Samia passed 3,000.
body: With Lewis Pettis retired, the tackle race has a new challenger. A.T. Hoyer made 222 tackles in 17 games for the 6-11 Raiders and stands at 3,328, second on the league list. Travon Swaim, still playing in Detroit, added 149 of his own to reach 3,405, so the gap is 77. Both men are 34.

Hoyer is also 7 interceptions from Jamon Brooker's record of 47 after picking off 3 more, and his card rose 29% on the season. In Denver, Akayleb Samia made 218 tackles and passed 3,000 for his career, finishing at 3,047.

One chase ended without a finish line. Ryland Maxwell retired 18 rushing touchdowns short of Lane McCoy, so the league mark of 458 stays with McCoy. And the sack list has a new leader in Snoop Dotson, whose 26 put him 2 clear of Deshone Bello and Kalif Suh.

articles.headline: Green Bay Ends Its Long Skid Against Skura, and the Giants Fall to 0-20
articles.dek: The Packers handed the Bears their only loss of the season. The Giants and Commanders both lost to Chicago in the playoffs.
body: The move to Chicago put the Packers in Skura's division, and they were the only club to beat him. Green Bay won 25-22 at home in week 5, ending a run of 10 straight wins by Skura's clubs over the Packers that stretched back to the Y88 conference round. The Bears answered 38-32 in Chicago in week 13, and the series now stands at 11-1.

The old NFC East rivals followed him into the postseason. The Giants went 12-5 and lost 46-25 in Chicago in the divisional round. In 20 recorded meetings with Skura's clubs since Y88 they have never won.

Washington, also 12-5, lost twice: 30-13 at home in week 16 and 40-29 in the conference round. Skura's clubs now lead that series 14-5-1. A year earlier Washington had beaten Philadelphia 33-32. Chicago gave them nothing.

articles.headline: Quick Hits
articles.dek: Upsets, blowouts, a 113-point shootout and the rest of the league in Y98.
body: Upset of the year: the 49ers, who finished 5-12, won 31-23 in week 4 at Washington, a 12-5 club.
The 3-14 Cardinals produced the biggest blowout of the season, 59-16 over those same 49ers in week 18.
Jacksonville won 62-51 in Seattle in week 12, 113 points in a single game.
Phillip Ball ran for 39 touchdowns for the 5-12 Saints, whose defense allowed 625 points, the most in the league.
Buffalo's Abraham Jack made 224 tackles and won his 3rd Defensive Player of the Year award; Arizona's Neal Johnson made 248, the most in the league.
The Rams scored 643 points, the most in the league, and Raphael Mosely's card rose 183% after 182 tackles.
Alijah Santos led the league with 1,765 rushing yards and scored 33 rushing touchdowns for Washington.

The Bears went 10-1 in one-score games in the regular season. By points scored and allowed they projected as an 11-win team, and they won 16.
Every Super Bowl the Dolphins have won came with Dorren Skura as their coach. Their Y98 final, a 40-38 loss, came against him.
Kristian Smoke scored on 27.1% of his catches as a first-year tight end: 19 touchdowns on 70 receptions.
Grant Isidora, 21, made 39 blocks in his first season, more than any other lineman in the league.
Eagles first-year back DeSean Fries ran for 25 touchdowns and fumbled 13 times in 18 games.
Brandon Jaclyde, 38, threw 5 interceptions in 21 games for Miami, 15 fewer than MVP JJ Starling.

value.tagline: The Eagles lose 4 games and win a sixth straight title anyway, 40-26 over the Bengals in Super Bowl CLV, Ryland Maxwell takes a 7th Super Bowl MVP at 34 and re-signs with Akiem Brock for one more run, and Grover Calitro scores 43 times.

articles.headline: Six Straight: Eagles Beat the Bengals 40-26 in Super Bowl CLV
articles.dek: Philadelphia lost 4 regular-season games, its most under Dorren Skura, and still won a sixth straight title as Ryland Maxwell took a 7th Super Bowl MVP at 34.
body: The losses came, and the trophy came anyway. Dorren Skura's Eagles went 13-4 in Y96, the most regular-season defeats in his nine seasons in Philadelphia, after records of 17-0, 15-2 and 17-0 in the three years before. Then they beat the Bengals 40-26 in Super Bowl CLV, the 155th edition of the game, for the club's sixth straight championship.

The core never left the field. Ryland Maxwell, Bones Crawford, Akiem Brock and Calvin Wingo II each played all 21 of Philadelphia's games, playoffs included. Maxwell ran for 2,574 yards, the most in the league. Crawford threw 52 touchdown passes, also the most. Wingo led every receiver with 2,096 yards, and Brock made 62 blocks when no other lineman made more than 33.

Cincinnati arrived with the hottest runner in the league. Grover Calitro had scored 43 rushing touchdowns, the most in a season on league cards, and Alshon Lazard had turned his career back around. The Bengals put up 26 points in the final. Philadelphia scored 40.

It was not a farewell. Maxwell, 34, won his 13th ring and was named Super Bowl MVP for the 7th time. Brock, also 34, won his 8th ring, and Crawford won his 8th as well. Then the runner and the blocker who had been on the field for every title of the run both re-signed with Skura for one more year, and they open Y97 at 35. The question for the rest of the league is an old one: how to beat this team while its two constants are still on the field.

articles.headline: Mad Max at 34: 2,574 Yards, a 7th Super Bowl MVP and One More Year
articles.dek: Ryland Maxwell's Y96 was one of his best. He has 32,108 career rushing yards, 13 rings and the highest Career Legacy on file, and he re-signed for Y97.
body: Most great runners fade at 34. Ryland Maxwell sped up. He ran for 2,574 yards, 670 more than anyone else in the league, and scored 25 rushing touchdowns in 21 games. He stands at 32,108 career yards, the league record, 7,601 clear of Lane McCoy's 24,507.

The touchdown list is the one race he has not won yet. Maxwell's 421 rushing touchdowns top Skura's record board but rank third in the league, 4 behind Siran Spector's 425 and 37 behind McCoy's 458. Everything else is already his: 125 career touchdown catches, 13 rings and 7 Super Bowl MVPs, the last two both the most on file.

His Career Legacy stands at 14,903, the highest on file, and the Hall of Fame watch scores him at 100, the maximum, far above the bar of 65. The Hall will have to wait. Skura re-signed him in Y96, and he opens Y97 at 35, still an Eagle. Every one of his rings came with Dorren Skura: 2 with the Jets, 5 with the Falcons and 6 with the Eagles. One ordinary season would carry him past Spector, and few backs have ever been given the chance to try at 35.

articles.headline: Akiem Brock Has 8 Rings, a Hall of Fame Case and One More Year to Play
articles.dek: The league's best blocker made 62 blocks in Y96 at 34, and he and Ryland Maxwell are both back for another run.
body: No lineman on league cards came near Akiem Brock in Y96, and none had for years. He made 62 blocks in 21 games, 29 more than JD Pircher of the Bengals or Caleb Linsley of the Giants, and passed 500 for his career on the way to 538 in 181 games.

He spent his whole card career in Philadelphia, and the rings followed: 8 of them, every one with Dorren Skura. In nine seasons together, Skura's Eagles won the title eight times. Y90 was the one that got away.

The Hall of Fame watch scores him at 97, the best standing among offensive linemen and well clear of the bar of 65; Maxwell's is 100, the maximum. His Career Legacy stands at 11,394 and his card at 29,312. He was 34 in Y96, the same age as Maxwell, and both re-signed with Skura to play Y97 at 35. Linemen rarely get the headlines in a dynasty built on a record-setting runner and a quarterback who threw 52 touchdown passes in Y96. When the vote does come, it will say what the box scores never could: the runner and the quarterback had help.

articles.headline: Leglue's MVP at 36 Is a Verdict on Crawford's 17 Interceptions
articles.dek: Bones Crawford threw 52 touchdown passes, 11 more than anyone, and led the league in interceptions for a third straight season. The award went to Detroit.
body: Margus Leglue has spent his whole card career in Detroit, and at 36 he finally won the league's top award. He threw for 3,803 yards and 41 touchdowns with 1 interception in 19 games and was named Most Valuable Player for the first time. His overall rose from 78 to 84 and his card from 237 to 874.

The case against Bones Crawford made itself. He threw 52 touchdown passes, the most in the league, and 17 interceptions, when no other quarterback threw more than 6. It was the third season in a row he led the league in interceptions, after 20 in Y94 and 10 in Y95, and this time the voters held it against him. His MVP count stays at 5.

The market took the other side. Crawford's card value rose 124.4% to 19,210, and he collected his 8th ring. Leglue has the trophy; Crawford has the jewellery and the price tag. One of them was the better quarterback in Y96, and the argument will outlast both careers.

articles.headline: Calitro's 43 Touchdowns Break the Season Mark and Carry Cincinnati to the Final
articles.dek: Grover Calitro passed Siran Spector's 42 for the most rushing touchdowns in a season on file, and Alshon Lazard found his game again. The Bengals fell 40-26 in Super Bowl CLV.
body: Two seasons ago Cincinnati went 6-11 and its young quarterback was a cautionary tale. In Y96 the Bengals were the last club standing between the Eagles and a sixth straight title, and they lost Super Bowl CLV 40-26.

Grover Calitro was the reason they got there. He ran for 1,904 yards, second only to Ryland Maxwell, and scored 43 rushing touchdowns, the most in a single season on league cards, one more than Siran Spector's 42 for Houston in Y89. Nobody else in the league scored more than 30. He played all 21 games.

Alshon Lazard threw 39 touchdown passes as a rookie in Y93 and fell to 18 a year later. In Y96 he found the middle: 3,749 yards, 33 touchdowns and 2 interceptions. Teair Dye, in his second season, made 225 tackles.

The critics will point to what Calitro did not win. The Offensive Player of the Year award went to Alton Yeldon of the Seahawks, who ran for 1,558 yards and 27 touchdowns. A record season and no trophy: Cincinnati will take the trip to the final instead.

articles.headline: Brooker Draws Level With Hobbs at 43, and Swaim Climbs to Third on the Tackle List
articles.dek: Jamon Brooker tied the career interception record, Lewis Pettis was shut out, and Ryland Maxwell sits 4 rushing touchdowns short of second place.
body: A year ago Jamon Brooker and Lewis Pettis were tied at 41 interceptions, 2 short of Damar Hobbs. Brooker got both in Y96. He picked off 2 passes for the Packers and now shares the career record of 43 with Hobbs. At 33, he needs one more to own it.
Pettis played all 17 of the Cowboys' games and did not intercept a pass. He stays at 41, though his overall still rose from 95 to 97.

Travon Swaim made 199 tackles for the Lions and reached 3,064, passing Kyron Atwell's 3,059 for third on the career list. Only K'Lavon Settle, at 3,185, and Terron Stidham, at 3,132, have more, and Swaim is 121 from the record.

Angelo Moton of the Packers scored 30 rushing touchdowns and passed 350 for his career. And the chase still open: Maxwell is at 421, 4 short of Spector's 425 for second on that list, and he is back for Y97.

articles.headline: Ty Lock's Long Goodbye, and the Rookie Who Took His Place
articles.dek: The Giants' quarterback since Y83 is retired after 330 games and 627 touchdown passes. Yurik Okudah threw 34 in his first season.
body: Ty Lock's retirement is now on the record, and his last snaps came in Y95, when he was 39. He played 330 games, threw for 68,237 yards and 627 touchdowns with 137 interceptions, and won 2 MVP awards. Both of his rings came early, with Dorren Skura's Jets, before a multi-team trade sent him to New York ahead of Y83.
New York was his home for thirteen seasons and never gave him a ring. From Y88 on, the obstacle was his old coach: by the end of Y95 the Giants had never once beaten Skura's Eagles.

His successor arrived ready. Yurik Okudah, a rookie, threw for 3,610 yards and 34 touchdowns with 2 interceptions in 19 games. His card sells for 23, the price of an unknown, but the market's skill grade already reads A+. Lock spent a career chasing Philadelphia. Okudah has time to start his own chase.

articles.headline: Rashawn Elder Catches 122 Passes, and the Class of Y95 Keeps Coming
articles.dek: A rookie tight end led the league in catches, Mario Lamb scored 28 times for the Chiefs, and Payton Jarrett has 2 rings in 2 seasons.
body: Twenty-one new players reached league cards in Y96. The busiest was Rashawn Elder of the Colts, a tight end who caught 122 passes, the most in the league, though for only 675 yards, 5.5 a catch. Mario Lamb ran for 1,463 yards and 28 touchdowns for the Chiefs, Damiere Norton threw 28 touchdown passes for the Patriots, and Rico Gee threw 25 with 1 interception for the Cowboys.

Last year's class did not slow down. Bryant Herbig threw 30 touchdown passes for the Commanders for the second straight season, Teair Dye made 225 tackles for the Bengals, and tight end Ulysees Howell caught 81 passes.

Payton Jarrett had the best of it again: 74 catches, 1,419 yards and 16 touchdowns, second in the league in receiving yards behind Calvin Wingo II for the second year running, and a 2nd ring in his 2nd season. His overall rose from 67 to 72 and his card from 13 to 37. It is still a bargain.

articles.headline: Quick Hits
articles.dek: A second Defensive Player of the Year award, a tight end's leap and a linebacker who led the league in sacks.
body: Abraham Jack of the Bills was Defensive Player of the Year for the 2nd time, with 237 tackles, tied with A.T. Hoyer of the Raiders for the most.
Alton Yeldon of the Seahawks was Offensive Player of the Year for the first time.
Jacob Proise's overall jumped from 84 to 93 and his card from 1,109 to 5,527 after 786 yards and 14 touchdown catches.
Snoop Dotson led the league with 4 sacks and 2 forced fumbles, added 5 interceptions and won his 7th ring.
Lenny Baun of the Dolphins intercepted 6 passes, the most in the league.
Calvin Wingo II caught 104 passes for 2,096 yards and 18 touchdowns, the most receiving yards in the league for a second straight season.

value.tagline: The Eagles go 15-2 and beat the Colts 38-22 in Super Bowl CLVI for a seventh straight title, Bones Crawford throws 64 touchdown passes for a 6th MVP, and Ryland Maxwell, 35, wins an 8th Super Bowl MVP.

articles.headline: Seven Straight: Eagles Beat the Colts 38-22 in Super Bowl CLVI
articles.dek: Philadelphia went 15-2, allowed the fewest points in the league and won a seventh straight title as Ryland Maxwell took his 8th Super Bowl MVP at 35.
body: There was no slippage this time. A year after a 13-4 regular season, Dorren Skura's Eagles went 15-2 in Y97, 8-0 at home, and outscored their opponents by 221 points. Then they beat the Packers 40-15, the Seahawks 32-21 and, in Super Bowl CLVI, the Colts 38-22. It is the club's seventh straight championship, a run that began the season after the Y90 final loss to the Texans.

The offense was a quarterback at his peak throwing to two receivers at once. Bones Crawford threw 64 touchdown passes, 25 more than anyone else, and was named MVP for the 6th time. Calvin Wingo II caught passes for 2,158 yards and Payton Jarrett for 2,007; the next best receiver in the league finished with 895. The defense allowed 358 points, the fewest in the league.

The old guard held. Ryland Maxwell, 35, missed 2 of the 20 games through injury and still led the league with 1,847 rushing yards. He took his career rushing touchdowns to 440, second on the league list, and was named Super Bowl MVP for the 8th time. Akiem Brock, also 35, made 43 blocks, 9 more than any other lineman, and won his 9th ring alongside Crawford.

The two losses told their own story. Both came against division rivals: 38-28 in Dallas to a Cowboys team that finished 5-11-1, and 33-32 in Washington. Both were answered in Philadelphia later in the season. For a dynasty still built around a 35-year-old runner and a 35-year-old blocker, the question for Y98 is no longer whether the Eagles can win, but how long those two can keep playing.

articles.headline: Mad Max at 35: 1,847 Yards, an 8th Super Bowl MVP and the First 50,000 Card
articles.dek: Ryland Maxwell led the league in rushing again, passed Siran Spector on the career touchdown list and is now 18 short of Lane McCoy's league mark.
body: Age has not found Ryland Maxwell yet. At 35 he ran for 1,847 yards, the most in the league and 150 more than Seattle's Alton Yeldon, and scored 19 rushing touchdowns plus 5 more as a receiver. Injury cost him 2 of Philadelphia's 20 games. It did not cost him the rushing title.

The career yardage record was already his; now it is out of sight. He stands at 33,955 rushing yards, the league mark, 9,448 clear of McCoy. The touchdown list is different. His 440 rushing touchdowns top Skura's record board and passed Spector's 425, but the league mark still belongs to McCoy at 458, 18 away. At his Y97 pace that is about one more healthy season.

The postseason was his as well. Maxwell was named Super Bowl MVP for the 8th time and won his 14th ring, every one of them with Dorren Skura. The market has noticed: his card is worth 50,066, the first in the market's history to pass 50,000, and 8,821 more than Sherman Brandson's, the next most valuable.

articles.headline: The Doctor Answers Back: 64 Touchdown Passes and a 6th MVP
articles.dek: A year after Margus Leglue's MVP was read as a verdict on his 17 interceptions, Bones Crawford threw for 4,857 yards and took the award back.
body: Last season's argument was about turnovers. This season's was about everything else. Crawford threw for 4,857 yards, 883 more than Jacksonville's Kalif Risner, and 64 touchdowns, 25 more than Baltimore's Bryant Cronk in second place. He played all 20 of Philadelphia's games, and the MVP came back to him for the 6th time.

The interceptions did not go away. He threw 15, more than twice the 7 thrown by Cronk, the next most in the league, and the Eagles won anyway: a quarterback throwing to Calvin Wingo II and Payton Jarrett can afford a few mistakes. He now has 610 career touchdown passes and 49,651 yards in 192 games, and 9 rings.
Leglue did not fade so much as get outgunned. At 37 the Lions quarterback threw 37 touchdown passes for a 12-5 club. It was a fine season. It was not 64.

articles.headline: Wingo 2,158, Jarrett 2,007: Philadelphia's Receivers Lap the League
articles.dek: Calvin Wingo II was Offensive Player of the Year for the 3rd time. Payton Jarrett, 23, caught 23 touchdowns and the longest pass on Skura's record board.
body: Most clubs would settle for one receiver like this. Philadelphia had two. Wingo caught 109 passes for 2,158 yards and 22 touchdowns; Jarrett caught 100 for 2,007 and 23. The next most productive receiver in the league, Dallas's Taco Coulter, finished with 895 yards.
Wingo's 3rd Offensive Player of the Year award came with his 7th ring. His OVR rose to 96 and his card's value climbed 42.3% to 4,651.

Jarrett is the part that should worry the rest of the league. In week 15 against the Ravens he caught a throw from Bones Crawford that travelled 32 yards in the air, the longest on Skura's record board. His card rose from 37 to 92, and the market's skill grade moved from A+ to S. He is 23 and already owns 3 rings.

articles.headline: Akiem Brock at 35: 43 Blocks, a 9th Ring and No Lineman Close
articles.dek: The league's best blocker came back for one more season, played every game and finished with an OVR of 99.
body: Akiem Brock was 34 when Y96 ended, and he re-signed for one more year instead of retiring. Philadelphia got its money's worth. He made 43 blocks in all 20 of the Eagles' games, 9 more than Seattle's Perrion Randall and 10 more than Washington's Victor Brandel, and his OVR rose to 99.

He now has 581 career blocks in 201 games and 9 rings, every one of them won with Dorren Skura in Philadelphia. That ties him with Bones Crawford, and among the Eagles only Ryland Maxwell, with 14, has more.

The market keeps climbing with him. His card rose 13.7% to 33,323, behind only Maxwell among players still on a club. Linemen rarely carry a dynasty's headlines, but the two most valuable cards among active players both belong to Philadelphia: the runner, and the man who blocks for him.

articles.headline: Brooker Takes the Interception Record at 47, and Pettis Closes on Swaim
articles.dek: Green Bay's Jamon Brooker pulled 4 clear of Damar Hobbs and Lewis Pettis. Pettis is 67 tackles from the career mark, and Snoop Dotson is 1 sack from a share of second place.
body: The interception record changed hands without a ceremony. Jamon Brooker began Y97 level with Damar Hobbs at 43, picked off 4 passes for the 12-5 Packers and finished at 47, the most on league cards. Lewis Pettis of Dallas also reached 43, so the two men behind Brooker now share second.

Pettis has a bigger prize in sight. He made 200 tackles in all 17 of the Cowboys' games and stands at 3,189. The problem is that Travon Swaim is still playing too: he added 192 of his own in Detroit, so the gap only shrank from 75 to 67. Both men are 34.

In Philadelphia, Snoop Dotson added 1 sack and an 8th ring, though injury cost him 1 of the Eagles' 20 games. He has 23 career sacks, 1 behind the 24 that Deshone Bello and Kalif Suh share, second only to the 112 on Skura's record board.

articles.headline: Twelfth in the Power Rankings, Last Team Standing in the AFC: Inside the Colts' Run
articles.dek: Indianapolis went 10-7, finished third in its own division and won three playoff games behind a 21-year-old quarterback in his first season.
body: Nobody picked Indianapolis. The Colts finished 10-7, 12th in the power rankings and behind both the 12-4-1 Titans and the 10-6-1 Jaguars in their own division. Then they won three playoff games to reach Super Bowl CLVI, and they played 21 games in all, more than any club in the league.

Jackson Poyer, 21, ran the offense in his first season on league cards and threw for 3,565 yards and 29 touchdowns with just 2 interceptions. River Kuechly ran for 1,659 yards and 31 touchdowns, and Rashawn Elder, 22, caught 119 passes, the most in the league. Reggie Deayon led the defense with 225 tackles.

The final is where the run ran out. The Eagles scored 38 and won by 16. Still, the Colts have their quarterback. Poyer's card sells for 18, the price of an unknown, but his Career Legacy already stands at 3,825 after one season.

articles.headline: From the Super Bowl to 7-10: Cincinnati Falls Back to the Pack
articles.dek: Grover Calitro went from 43 rushing touchdowns to 16, and the Bengals' best day of the season came 55-10 against the Jets.
body: A year ago the Bengals were in the Super Bowl and Grover Calitro had just scored more rushing touchdowns in a season than anyone on league cards. In Y97 Cincinnati went 7-10, scored 489 points, allowed exactly 489 and finished 21st in the power rankings.

Calitro played all 17 games and still fell off a cliff: 1,116 yards and 16 touchdowns, after 1,904 yards and 43 touchdowns the season before. The market's skill grade slipped from B+ to B. Alshon Lazard threw for 3,042 yards and 24 touchdowns with 1 interception, tidy numbers that never turned into a winning record.

The one afternoon that looked like Y96 came in week 8, a 55-10 win at the Jets, the biggest blowout of the season. The Jets, the club Dorren Skura coached before Atlanta and Philadelphia, finished 5-12.

articles.headline: Two Losses, Two Rivals: Dallas and Washington Finally Draw Blood
articles.dek: The 5-11-1 Cowboys pulled off the upset of the season and Washington won by a point. The Giants are still waiting for their first win over Skura's Eagles.
body: Philadelphia lost only twice in Y97, and both defeats came inside the NFC East. In week 6 the Cowboys, on their way to a 5-11-1 finish, beat the Eagles 38-28 in Dallas, the biggest upset of the league season by the records of the two clubs.

In week 11 it was Washington's turn. Bryant Herbig's Commanders won 33-32 at home, the only one-score game the Eagles lost all season. Herbig threw 34 touchdown passes with 1 interception for an 11-6 club that has now beaten Skura's Eagles 5 times in their recorded meetings since Y88.

Both debts were paid in Philadelphia: 34-23 over Dallas in week 14 and 40-20 over Washington in week 17. The Giants lost 30-18 and 40-21 and have still never beaten Skura's Eagles in a recorded meeting. New York did win the wildest game of the year, 54-51 at Tampa Bay in week 17, with Yurik Okudah throwing 28 touchdown passes in 17 games.

articles.headline: Quick Hits
articles.dek: Around the league in Y97.
body: Denver's Akayleb Samia made 242 tackles, and his card more than doubled, up 165.6% to 5,060.
Jacoby Nunez, 21, led the league with 249 tackles for the 4-13 Panthers in his first season on league cards.
Seattle's Alton Yeldon led the league with 33 rushing touchdowns, and Buffalo's Chandon Liedtke, 21, scored 32.
Buffalo scored 621 points, the most in the league, and went 11-6.
Atlanta's Tramon Holton, 31, was Defensive Player of the Year with 210 tackles for a 9-8 Falcons club.
Three games ended in ties, among them a 37-37 draw between the Cardinals and the Jaguars in week 12.
The Chiefs lost 40-8 at home to the Eagles in week 9, Philadelphia's biggest win of the season.
The Raiders went 3-14 and finished last in the power rankings.

The Eagles allowed 358 points in Y97, the fewest in the league and 50 fewer than the 12-5 Patriots, the next stingiest club.
